description: Use this for (a) one source against multiple targets in a single call ('USD vs EUR, GBP, JPY'), or (b) the rate at a specific past datetime ('EUR/USD at 2025-03-14T12:00Z'), optionally bucketed by hour/day/week/month. Returns { rates: [{ rate, source, target, time }, ...] } — one row per target × time bucket. For a single live pair use get_exchange_rate. For fixed lookback windows (1d/7d/30d/1y ending now) use get_historical_rates.

group.description: Aggregation bucket: 'hour', 'day', 'week', or 'month'. Useful when time is omitted to return rolling averages. Omit for raw single-point output.

source.description: ISO 4217 currency code, 3 letters, case-insensitive (e.g. 'USD', 'EUR', 'GBP', 'JPY'). For a source/target pair, the returned rate is how much 1 unit of source is worth in target. Fiat only — no crypto, no commodities. Call list_currencies if unsure whether a code is supported.

target.description: One or more ISO 4217 codes, comma-separated, no spaces, case-insensitive. Examples: 'EUR' (single) or 'EUR,GBP,JPY' (multi). Each target becomes a separate row in the response.

time.description: Single point-in-time ISO 8601 UTC timestamp (e.g. '2025-03-14T12:00:00Z'). Omit for the latest rate.

name: get_rates_authenticated
title: Get multi-target or point-in-time rates
